nba5642b6812.s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Gram Panchayats Act, dealing with the village level, enacted?
nba5642b6812.x: The AP Gram Panchayats Act came in 1964; the AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act was 1959 and the Mandal system 1986.

n0e3a4be70af.s: Under the 1986 reforms of the N.T. Rama Rao Government, Panchayat Samithis in Andhra Pradesh were replaced by:
n0e3a4be70af.x: In 1986 Panchayat Samithis became Mandal Praja Parishads, while Zilla Parishads were renamed Zilla Praja Parishads.

n3bcab6c40ab.s: Which Article of the Constitution recognises the Gram Sabha?
n3bcab6c40ab.x: Article 243A recognises the Gram Sabha, whose powers and functions are fixed by State law.

na48e9c318b5.s: Grades of municipalities (Special, Selection, Grade I, II, III) under the AP Municipalities Act are fixed on the basis of:
na48e9c318b5.x: Municipalities in AP are graded Special, Selection, Grade I, II and III by annual income.

ncd5784f2127.s: The 33.33% BC reservation in AP urban local bodies is implemented under the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the:
ncd5784f2127.x: The urban BC quota runs under the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the AP Municipalities Act, 1965, not the Panchayat Raj Act.

nf9c50420eee.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 is known for:
o: Removing the two-child norm for municipal polls
nf9c50420eee.x: The 2024 Bill, passed without debate, removed the two-child norm, reversing an earlier restriction. The Uniform Mutation Fee came with the Third Amendment Bill 2026.

n1025e8e2456.s: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor for a term of:
n1025e8e2456.x: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor for five years and has the status of a High Court Judge.

n4fe6afae0cb.s: The 'mixed scanning' model of policy-making was propounded by:
n4fe6afae0cb.x: Etzioni propounded mixed scanning; Lindblom gave incrementalism and Simon bounded rationality.

nbc27cda5069.s: Which of the following is a remedy, not a cause, of policy failure?
nbc27cda5069.x: Real-time outcome tracking is a remedy; weak coordination, poor targeting and resource shortfalls cause policy failure.

n9323d8af3b8.s: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) was introduced in India from:
n9323d8af3b8.x: DBT began on 1 January 2013; it cuts ghost beneficiaries and middlemen but may exclude people without digital access.

nindian-society-7-14.s: Which of the following communities is NOT dealt with by the Ministry of Minority Affairs?
nindian-society-7-14.x: Minority Affairs covers Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains; Hindus are not a notified national minority.

nc0a66ec4add.s: Social welfare services are primarily targeted at:
o: All citizens on a universal basis
Vulnerable groups such as the disabled, widows and destitute children
nc0a66ec4add.x: Social welfare means targeted services for vulnerable groups; general health services for all are not a targeted welfare service.

nf1d132e9142.s: Rehabilitation in deviant or vulnerable situations such as drugs, beggary and juvenile delinquency is called:
nf1d132e9142.x: Social defence is rehabilitation in deviant or vulnerable situations; social justice aims at ending social and economic inequalities.

n5ddd562a3c1.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n5ddd562a3c1.x: Social welfare is short-term and consumption-oriented; social development is long-term and production-oriented.

n86e0edc4764.s: The typology of ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears about judicial activism was given by:
n86e0edc4764.x: Upendra Baxi gave this typology of fears; it does not include an 'electoral' fear.

n8f05e6dcf8c.s: Press briefings and accreditation of journalists in India are handled by the:
n8f05e6dcf8c.x: The PIB handles briefings, accreditation and social-media communication; the PM's Communication Wing is a separate body for PMO and Cabinet publicity.

n4de31fc91e5.s: Which of the following is a recognised concern about the bureaucracy as a policy actor?
o: Removal of PSC members by Parliament
No role in drafting Government Bills
Discretion at the front line of implementation
n4de31fc91e5.x: Frontline implementation discretion is a concern; the bureaucracy does draft Bills, and PSC members are removed after a Supreme Court inquiry.

n616a0413c02.s: Members of a Public Service Commission can be removed for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the:
n616a0413c02.x: PSC members are removed for misbehaviour after an inquiry by the Supreme Court, not Parliament.

new.s: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959 at:
new.x: Panchayati Raj was inaugurated at Nagaur, not Jaipur, on 2 October 1959.

new.s: Which committee recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj system of Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat?
new.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78) recommended two tiers; Balwant Rai Mehta recommended three.

new.s: Which committee described Panchayati Raj Institutions as 'grass without roots'?
new.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) called PRIs 'grass without roots'.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: L.M. Singhvi Committee – Gram Sabha as direct democracy
new.x: L.M. Singhvi (1986) saw the Gram Sabha as direct democracy and sought constitutional recognition; G.V.K. Rao said 'grass without roots' and Ashok Mehta proposed two tiers.

new.s: How many sections does the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (Act 13 of 1994) contain?
new.x: The AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 has 278 sections in 8 Parts.

new.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Zilla Parishad Chairperson is elected:
o: Indirectly from among the ZPTC members
By the Sarpanches of the district
new.x: The ZP Chairperson is elected indirectly from among the directly elected ZPTC members.

new.s: After district reorganisation, the 13 Zilla Praja Parishads of Andhra Pradesh became:
new.x: The 13 Zilla Praja Parishads were reorganised into 28, not 26.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the three tiers under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994?
o: The Mandal Parishad President is elected indirectly
The intermediate tier is the Panchayat Samiti
Each tier has a five-year term
new.x: AP's intermediate tier is the Mandal Parishad, not the Panchayat Samiti; the other statements are correct.

new.s: Which of the following is a discretionary function of a Gram Panchayat?
new.x: Libraries are discretionary; burial grounds, drinking water and street lighting are obligatory functions.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about a Gram Panchayat in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Sarpanch convenes Gram Panchayat meetings.
2. The Sarpanch is the elected head who presides.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Sarpanch is the elected, presiding head, but meetings are convened by the Panchayat Secretary, so statement 1 is wrong.

new.s: The original State Election Commission of Andhra Pradesh was formed on:
new.x: The original AP SEC was formed on 17 June 1994; after bifurcation the residuary State's SEC was constituted on 30 January 2016.

new.s: Reservation for women in local bodies is at least:
new.x: Women get at least one-third of seats; SC/ST seats are by population and by rotation.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the unanimous-election incentives for Gram Panchayats announced in January 2021:
1. ₹5 lakh was offered where the population is below 2,000.
2. ₹15 lakh was offered where the population is above 10,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: above 10,000 the incentive was ₹20 lakh; ₹15 lakh was for 5,001-10,000.

new.s: The 2021 Gram Panchayat elections in Andhra Pradesh were held in how many phases?
new.x: The 2021 panchayat polls were held in four phases in January-February 2021.

new.s: Who is the present State Election Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh, appointed in April 2026?
new.x: Anil Chandra Punetha was appointed AP State Election Commissioner in April 2026.

new.s: The State Finance Commission for local bodies is constituted every five years by the:
new.x: The SFC (Articles 243I/243Y) is formed by the Governor, not the SEC.

new.s: The 5th State Finance Commission of Andhra Pradesh was constituted on 20 March 2023 for the period:
new.x: The 5th AP SFC was constituted on 20 March 2023 to report for 2025-30.

new.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, which local bodies alone become eligible for grants?
o: Bodies with own revenue over ₹50 lakh
new.x: Only duly constituted local bodies get grants, so about ₹12,150 crore is at risk if AP polls slip past October 2026.

new.s: According to the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how many urban local bodies does Andhra Pradesh have?
new.x: AP has 123 ULBs: 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats.

new.s: How many Municipal Corporations are there in Andhra Pradesh as per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26?
new.x: AP has 17 Municipal Corporations among its 123 ULBs.

new.s: Under Article 243Q, a Nagar Panchayat is constituted for:
new.x: A Nagar Panchayat is for a transitional area; municipalities and corporations are for smaller and larger urban areas.

new.s: Besides the Council headed by the Mayor and the Commissioner, an AP Municipal Corporation has:
new.x: A Corporation consists of the Council (Mayor), Standing Committees and the Commissioner.

new.s: Which Municipal Corporation in Andhra Pradesh has zonal commissioners under its Municipal Commissioner?
new.x: GVMC has zonal commissioners working under the Municipal Commissioner.

new.s: The APCRDA, for the Amaravati capital region, was created under an Act of:
new.x: APCRDA works under the APCRDA Act 2014; VMRDA for Visakhapatnam came in 2018.

new.s: Who, as Minister of Municipal Administration and Urban Development, piloted the AP Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024?
new.x: Minister P. Narayana (MA&UD) moved the 2024 Bill that removed the two-child norm.

new.s: Until the AP Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026, Mayors in Andhra Pradesh were elected:
new.x: Mayors were so far elected indirectly; the Cabinet on 18 August 2026 approved their direct election.

new.s: PuraSeva, developed by the eGovernments Foundation, is a:
o: Municipal app for services and grievance redressal
new.x: PuraSeva is a municipal app for services and grievance redressal; Mee Seva is the single-window counter.

new.s: The Village/Ward Secretariat system works in relation to the Gram Panchayat:
o: As a replacement for the Gram Panchayat
new.x: Launched on 2 October 2019, a secretariat for each village or ward cluster works alongside the Gram Panchayat.

new.s: Which AP panchayat won the first prize (women-friendly) at the National Panchayat Awards 2026?
new.x: Bokkasampalem (Srikalahasti, Tirupati) came first in the women-friendly category; five AP panchayats won in 2026.

new.s: On 1 April 2026, Andhra Pradesh won which awards for the second year running?
o: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas awards
Nanaji Deshmukh Gaurav Gram Sabha awards
new.x: AP won the Deen Dayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas awards for the second year running.

new.s: How many AP panchayats won National Panchayat Awards in 2026?
new.x: Five AP panchayats won the 2026 National Panchayat Awards, presented around National Panchayati Raj Day (24 April).

new.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the 'policy sciences'?
new.x: Harold Lasswell founded the policy sciences; Dye and Easton are known for their definitions.

new.s: Public policy as a 'purposive course of action' by actors dealing with a problem was defined by:
new.x: James Anderson defined policy as a purposive course of action followed by actors dealing with a problem.

new.s: Under Lowi's classification, PM-KISAN is an example of which type of policy?
new.x: PM-KISAN is distributive: benefits go to specific groups while costs are borne by all.

new.s: Land reforms and progressive income tax are examples of which Lowi policy type?
new.x: Redistributive policies transfer from one group to another, as land reforms and progressive income tax do.

new.s: Which of the following is the first stage of the policy cycle?
new.x: Agenda setting comes first; termination or revision is the last stage.

new.s: Communication and transparency in the policy cycle are important at:
new.x: Communication and transparency run through every stage of the policy cycle, not only evaluation.

new.s: The elite theory of policy-making, with the idea of the 'power elite', is associated with:
new.x: C. Wright Mills gave the 'power elite'; Bentley is linked with group theory and Easton with the systems model.

new.s: Group theory of public policy is associated with:
new.x: Group theory is linked with Arthur Bentley and David Truman.

new.s: The systems model of policy, with inputs, conversion, outputs and feedback, was given by:
new.x: David Easton gave the systems model as well as the definition 'authoritative allocation of values'.

new.s: Production Linked Incentives (PLI) are an example of which policy instrument?
new.x: PLI incentives and DBT subsidy reform illustrate taxes and subsidies as an instrument.

new.s: Running schools and Primary Health Centres is an example of which policy instrument?
new.x: Schools and PHCs are direct provision by the State.

new.s: Michael Lipsky's work on 'street-level bureaucracy' appeared in:
new.x: Lipsky's street-level bureaucracy dates to 1980; Pressman and Wildavsky's 'Implementation' was 1973.

new.s: From which date has Andhra Pradesh published Action Taken Reports on seven white papers as a remedy for implementation gaps?
new.x: AP has published Action Taken Reports on seven white papers from 22 June 2026.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh set up the independent social audit body SSAAT in:
new.x: AP began statewide NREGS social audits in 2006 and set up the independent SSAAT in 2009.

new.s: The JAM trinity links Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and:
new.x: JAM links Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile for Direct Benefit Transfer.

new.s: The Factories Act, 1948 is an example of which type of social legislation?
new.x: The Factories Act is protective, guarding against exploitation; the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 is regulatory.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of social legislation and its type is correctly matched?
new.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act is regulatory; the Factories Act is protective, the Minimum Wages Act regulatory and RTI enabling.

new.s: Which Directive Principle provides for a living wage for workers?
new.x: Article 43 provides a living wage; Article 42 covers humane work conditions and maternity relief.

new.s: Which Article of the Directive Principles deals with nutrition, living standards and public health?
new.x: Article 47 deals with nutrition, living standards and public health.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Directive Principles as a welfare mandate:
1. Article 42 provides for maternity relief.
2. Article 46 promotes the interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections.
3. Article 41 provides for a living wage for workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Articles 42 and 46 are correctly described; the living wage is in Article 43, while Article 41 covers right to work, education and public assistance.

new.s: Under the RTE Act, 2009, free schooling is guaranteed to children of the age group:
new.x: The RTE Act (Article 21A) guarantees free schooling for ages 6-14, not 6-18.

new.s: Under the RTI Act, 2005, information must normally be supplied within:
new.x: The RTI Act guarantees information within 30 days.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a social development programme?
new.x: Look East Policy is a foreign policy; Mid-Day Meal, SSA and the Rural Health Mission are social development programmes.

new.s: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was split off from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in:
new.x: Tribal Affairs was split off in 1999, a year after the Ministry of Welfare was renamed MoSJE (1998).

new.s: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was carved out on:
new.x: Minority Affairs was carved out on 29 January 2006; WCD also became a separate ministry in 2006.

new.s: During which Five-Year Plans did India's approach shift to empowerment?
new.x: The 6th Plan moved women from welfare to development; the 8th-9th Plans stressed empowerment.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Union welfare ministries?
o: Tribal Affairs deals with PESA implementation
WCD deals with ICDS and Poshan
Minority Affairs deals with transgender welfare
new.x: Transgender welfare is with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not Minority Affairs.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NITI Aayog?
o: It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015
It is chaired by the Prime Minister
new.x: NITI Aayog is non-constitutional and non-statutory; the other statements are correct.

new.s: The Cabinet Secretariat, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, functions directly under the:
new.x: The Cabinet Secretariat is directly under the PM and runs the Transaction of Business Rules.

new.s: The Muslim Women Act, 1986 was enacted by Parliament after which Supreme Court judgment?
new.x: Parliament passed the Muslim Women Act 1986 after Shah Bano; the SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018 followed Subhash Kashinath Mahajan.

new.s: An advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on a Presidential reference is given under:
new.x: An Article 143 reference yields only an advisory opinion, which is not binding.

new.s: The Prakash Singh (2006) guidelines of the Supreme Court relate to:
new.x: Prakash Singh (2006) laid down police reforms, including fixed DGP tenure.

new.s: Civil Services Boards and fixed tenure for civil servants were directed in which case?
new.x: T.S.R. Subramanian (2013) directed Civil Services Boards and fixed tenure.

new.s: Public Interest Litigation in India rests on which constitutional provisions?
new.x: PIL is based on Articles 32, 226 and 142.

new.s: The Right to Food PIL filed by PUCL in 2001 eventually led to the:
new.x: The PUCL Right to Food PIL (2001) led to the NFSA 2013.

new.s: The Right to Work campaign and the National Advisory Council are associated with which law?
new.x: The Right to Work campaign with the NAC produced MGNREGA 2005.

new.s: The Centre for Policy Research (CPR) and NCAER are examples of which type of think tank?
new.x: CPR and NCAER are independent think tanks, not government bodies.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of think tank and its type is correctly matched?
new.x: The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation is Congress-linked; CPR and NCAER are independent and the National Innovation Council (2010) is a government body.

new.s: The 33.33% BC quota in AP urban local bodies was given effect through:
new.x: The NDA's 2024 poll promise became policy through G.O. Rt. No. 1065 (August 2026).
